# invoicing

Small helpers for building and printing customer invoices. Standard library only.

## Modules

- `invoicing.money`: `Decimal` money helpers. Amounts are rounded to whole cents with halves rounded
  **up, away from zero** (`0.125 -> 0.13`, `-0.125 -> -0.13`), matching the printed invoices. Floats are
  rejected; pass strings, ints or `Decimal`s.
- `invoicing.pricing`: line pricing. Lines of **10 or more units** get a 5% bulk discount; the discounted
  line amount is rounded to the cent.
- `invoicing.currency`: exchange rates (`RATES`, in units of the currency per 1 EUR). `to_eur(amount, currency)`
  gives the EUR value rounded to the cent (used for EUR reporting). `convert(amount, src, dst)` converts at full
  precision through EUR (`amount / RATES[src] * RATES[dst]`) and rounds to the cent **once, at the end**.
- `invoicing.invoice`: `Invoice` (subtotal, VAT at 20% by default, total, `total_eur()` for reporting) and
  `paginate(lines, per_page)`, which splits invoice lines into printed pages of at most `per_page` lines, in
  order. Every line appears on exactly one page; an invoice with no lines has no pages. An invoice has a
  currency (EUR by default); a line can be priced in another currency, in which case its line amount (priced as
  above, in the price currency) is converted to the invoice currency with `convert`.

inv.add("Widget", 12, "2.50")
inv.add("Shipping", 1, "4.99")
inv.add("Adapter", 2, "7.35", price_currency="GBP")
print(inv.subtotal(), inv.tax(), inv.total())

import configparser
import sys
import unittest

CONFIG = "setup.cfg"


def discovery_settings(path=CONFIG):
    cfg = configparser.ConfigParser()
    cfg.read(path)
    start_dir = cfg.get("tool:unittest", "start_dir", fallback="tests")
    pattern = cfg.get("tool:unittest", "pattern", fallback="test_*.py")
    return start_dir, pattern


def main():
    start_dir, pattern = discovery_settings()
    suite = unittest.TestLoader().discover(start_dir, pattern=pattern, top_level_dir=".")
    result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(suite)
    return 0 if result.wasSuccessful() else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":

"""Small CSV parsing helper used by the reporting scripts."""


def parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into a list of records, each a list of field strings."""
    rows = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line == "":
            continue
        rows.append(line.split(","))
    return rows

final_files.README.md:
# csvparse

`csvparse.parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]` turns CSV text into a list of records, where each record is a
list of field strings.

## Supported format

- The delimiter is always a comma (`,`).
- A field may be wrapped in double quotes. The surrounding quotes are not part of the value.
- Inside a quoted field, commas and newlines are literal characters, and `""` stands for one `"` character.
- Unquoted fields never contain `"`, `,`, `\r` or `\n`.
- Records end with `\n` or `\r\n`. The line ending is not part of any field.
- A trailing line ending at the end of the input does not create an extra empty record; the last record may
  also have no line ending at all.
- Empty fields are empty strings (`a,,c` gives `["a", "", "c"]`; `""` is also an empty field).
- Whitespace is kept exactly as written; fields are never trimmed.
- Empty input gives `[]`.
- All values are returned as strings. There are no other dialect options (no other delimiters, no type
  conversion, no header handling, no comment lines).

## Tests

Run `python -B run_tests.py`. Each `tests/fixtures/NAME.csv` has a matching `tests/fixtures/NAME.json`
holding the expected list of records.

"""Small CSV parsing helper used by the reporting scripts."""


def parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into a list of records, each a list of field strings."""
    rows = []
    for line in text.split("\n"):
        if line == "":
            continue
        rows.append(line.split(","))
    return rows

final_files.README.md:
# csvparse

`csvparse.parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]` turns CSV text into a list of records, where each record is a
list of field strings.

## Supported format

- The delimiter is always a comma (`,`).
- A field may be wrapped in double quotes. The surrounding quotes are not part of the value.
- Inside a quoted field, commas and newlines are literal characters, and `""` stands for one `"` character.
- Unquoted fields never contain `"`, `,`, `\r` or `\n`.
- Records end with `\n` or `\r\n`. The line ending is not part of any field.
- A trailing line ending at the end of the input does not create an extra empty record; the last record may
  also have no line ending at all.
- Empty fields are empty strings (`a,,c` gives `["a", "", "c"]`; `""` is also an empty field).
- Whitespace is kept exactly as written; fields are never trimmed.
- Empty input gives `[]`.
- All values are returned as strings. There are no other dialect options (no other delimiters, no type
  conversion, no header handling, no comment lines).

## Tests

Run `python -B run_tests.py`. Each `tests/fixtures/NAME.csv` has a matching `tests/fixtures/NAME.json`
holding the expected list of records.

# invoicing

Small helpers for building and printing customer invoices. Standard library only.

## Modules

- `invoicing.money`: `Decimal` money helpers. Amounts are rounded to whole cents with halves rounded
  **up, away from zero** (`0.125 -> 0.13`, `-0.125 -> -0.13`), matching the printed invoices. Floats are
  rejected; pass strings, ints or `Decimal`s.
- `invoicing.pricing`: line pricing. Lines of **10 or more units** get a 5% bulk discount; the discounted
  line amount is rounded to the cent.
- `invoicing.currency`: exchange rates (`RATES`, in units of the currency per 1 EUR). `to_eur(amount, currency)`
  gives the EUR value rounded to the cent (used for EUR reporting). `convert(amount, src, dst)` converts at full
  precision through EUR (`amount / RATES[src] * RATES[dst]`) and rounds to the cent **once, at the end**.
- `invoicing.invoice`: `Invoice` (subtotal, VAT at 20% by default, total, `total_eur()` for reporting) and
  `paginate(lines, per_page)`, which splits invoice lines into printed pages of at most `per_page` lines, in
  order. Every line appears on exactly one page; an invoice with no lines has no pages. An invoice has a
  currency (EUR by default); a line can be priced in another currency, in which case its line amount (priced as
  above, in the price currency) is converted to the invoice currency with `convert`.

## Example

```python
from invoicing.invoice import Invoice

inv = Invoice("INV-0042")
inv.add("Widget", 12, "2.50")
inv.add("Shipping", 1, "4.99")
inv.add("Adapter", 2, "7.35", price_currency="GBP")
print(inv.subtotal(), inv.tax(), inv.total())
```

## Running the tests

    python -B run_tests.py

"""Run the invoicing test suite: python -B run_tests.py"""
import configparser
import sys
import unittest

CONFIG = "setup.cfg"


def discovery_settings(path=CONFIG):
    cfg = configparser.ConfigParser()
    cfg.read(path)
    start_dir = cfg.get("tool:unittest", "start_dir", fallback="tests")
    pattern = cfg.get("tool:unittest", "pattern", fallback="test_*.py")
    return start_dir, pattern


def main():
    start_dir, pattern = discovery_settings()
    suite = unittest.TestLoader().discover(start_dir, pattern=pattern, top_level_dir=".")
    result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(suite)
    return 0 if result.wasSuccessful() else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

from decimal import Decimal

from invoicing.invoice import Invoice, paginate

        inv.add("Widget", 2, "10.00")
        inv.add("Shipping", 1, "5.25")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("25.25"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.tax(), Decimal("5.05"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("30.30"))

    def test_empty_invoice(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-2")
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("0.00"))


class ForeignCurrencyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lines_priced_in_another_currency(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-3", currency="USD")
        inv.add("Adapter", 3, "4.99", price_currency="GBP")
        inv.add("Cable", 12, "12.50", price_currency="GBP")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("199.83"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.tax(), Decimal("39.97"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("239.80"))

    def test_mixed_currency_invoice(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-4", currency="GBP")
        inv.add("Licence", 1, "8.75", price_currency="USD")
        inv.add("Support", 1, "4.99", price_currency="CHF")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("11.43"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("13.72"))

    def test_chf_invoice(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-5", currency="CHF")
        inv.add("Licence", 1, "4.99", price_currency="USD")
        inv.add("Adapter", 1, "3.20", price_currency="GBP")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("7.86"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.tax(), Decimal("1.57"))


class PaginateTests(unittest.TestCase):

    def test_keeps_last_partial_page(self):
        self.assertEqual(paginate(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"], 2), [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"], ["e"]])

    def test_single_line(self):
        self.assertEqual(paginate(["a"], 3), [["a"]])

def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: P[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # P[0] = 0, P[1] = values[0], P[2] = values[0] + values[1], etc.
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for k in range(n):
        P[k + 1] = P[k] + values[k]
    
    # For each j, we need to count i < j such that lo <= P[j] - P[i] <= hi
    # Equivalently: P[j] - hi <= P[i] <= P[j] - lo
    # We'll use a Fenwick tree with coordinate compression
    
    # Collect all values we'll query: P values and P[j] - lo, P[j] - hi for each j
    coords = set(P)
    for p in P:
        coords.add(p - lo)
        coords.add(p - hi)
    
    sorted_coords = sorted(coords)
    coord_to_idx = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted_coords)}  # 1-indexed for BIT
    m = len(sorted_coords)
    
    # Fenwick tree operations
    bit = [0] * (m + 1)
    
    def bit_update(idx, delta):
        while idx <= m:
            bit[idx] += delta
            idx += idx & (-idx)
    
    def bit_query(idx):
        s = 0
        while idx > 0:
            s += bit[idx]
            idx -= idx & (-idx)
        return s
    
    def count_in_range(val_min, val_max):
        # Count number of inserted values in [val_min, val_max]
        # Find indices in sorted_coords

        right_idx = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_coords, val_max) - 1

        left_bit = left_idx + 1
        right_bit = right_idx + 1

    count = 0
    
    # Process each position
    # At step j, we've inserted P[0], ..., P[j-1] into the BIT
    # We want to count how many satisfy P[j] - hi <= P[i] <= P[j] - lo
    
    # First insert P[0]

        val_max = P[j] - lo
        count += count_in_range(val_min, val_max)

# span-sums

Small helpers for sums over contiguous spans of a sequence.

## `count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi)`

Returns the number of spans `values[i:j]` (`0 <= i < j <= len(values)`, i.e. non-empty runs of consecutive items)
whose sum `s` satisfies `lo <= s <= hi`. Spans at different positions count separately even if their contents are
equal.

- `values` is a list of ints (negative, zero or positive); `lo` and `hi` are ints. Both bounds are inclusive.
- An empty `values` returns `0`.
- `lo > hi` returns `0` (no sum can qualify).
- `values` is not modified.

```python
>>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)   # [1], [1, -2, 3], [-2, 3], [-2, 3, 1], [1]
5
```

## Tests and benchmark

runs the unit tests in `tests/`, then `bench.py`, which times `count_spans_with_sum_between` on the benchmark inputs in
`bench/inputs.json`, checks each result against `bench/expected.json`, and compares the time with the original
implementation kept in `bench/baseline.py`.

"""Run the unit tests in tests/, then the benchmark in bench.py."""
import importlib.util
import pathlib
import sys
import traceback

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))


def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run_unit_tests():
    passed = failed = 0
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "tests").glob("test_*.py")):
        try:
            module = load(path, path.stem)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"tests/{path.name} ERROR ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            continue
        for name, fn in list(vars(module).items()):
            if not (name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn)):
                continue
            try:
                fn()
            except Exception as exc:
                failed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} FAILED ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            else:
                passed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} PASSED")
    return passed, failed


def main():
    passed, failed = run_unit_tests()
    print()
    bench = load(ROOT / "bench.py", "bench")
    result = bench.main()
    print()

"""Benchmark count_spans_with_sum_between on bench/inputs.json against the original implementation (bench/baseline.py)."""
import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(main())

# csvparse

`csvparse.parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]` turns CSV text into a list of records, where each record is a
list of field strings.

## Supported format

- The delimiter is always a comma (`,`).
- A field may be wrapped in double quotes. The surrounding quotes are not part of the value.
- Inside a quoted field, commas and newlines are literal characters, and `""` stands for one `"` character.
- Unquoted fields never contain `"`, `,`, `\r` or `\n`.
- Records end with `\n` or `\r\n`. The line ending is not part of any field.
- A trailing line ending at the end of the input does not create an extra empty record; the last record may
  also have no line ending at all.
- Empty fields are empty strings (`a,,c` gives `["a", "", "c"]`; `""` is also an empty field).
- Whitespace is kept exactly as written; fields are never trimmed.
- Empty input gives `[]`.
- All values are returned as strings. There are no other dialect options (no other delimiters, no type
  conversion, no header handling, no comment lines).

## Tests

Run `python -B run_tests.py`. Each `tests/fixtures/NAME.csv` has a matching `tests/fixtures/NAME.json`
holding the expected list of records.

"""Run csvparse.parse over every fixture in tests/fixtures and compare with the expected records."""
import json
import sys
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURES = ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures"


def short(value, limit=160):
    text = json.dumps(value, default=repr)
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit] + "..."


def main():
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
    try:
        from csvparse import parse
    except Exception:
        print("ERROR importing csvparse.py")
        for line in traceback.format_exc().strip().splitlines()[-4:]:
            print("    " + line)
        print("========== 1 error ==========")
        return 1
    passed = failed = 0
    for csv_path in sorted(FIXTURES.glob("*.csv")):
        name = "tests/fixtures/" + csv_path.name
        with open(csv_path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text = fh.read()
        expected = json.loads(csv_path.with_suffix(".json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        try:
            got = parse(text)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(name + " FAILED")
            print("    " + type(exc).__name__ + ": " + str(exc)[:200])
            continue
        if got == expected:
            passed += 1
            print(name + " PASSED")
        else:
            failed += 1
            print(name + " FAILED")
            print("    input:    " + short(text))
            print("    expected: " + short(expected))
            print("    got:      " + short(got))
    if failed:
        print("========== %d failed, %d passed ==========" % (failed, passed))
    else:
        print("========== %d passed ==========" % passed)
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    return time.perf_counter() - start, out

"""Sums over contiguous spans of a sequence."""


def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: P[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # Then sum(values[i:j]) = P[j] - P[i]
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for k in range(n):
        P[k + 1] = P[k] + values[k]
    
    # Count pairs (i, j) with i < j such that lo <= P[j] - P[i] <= hi
    # This is equivalent to: P[j] - hi <= P[i] <= P[j] - lo
    count = 0
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        pj = P[j]
        min_pi = pj - hi
        max_pi = pj - lo
        for i in range(j):
            pi = P[i]
            if min_pi <= pi <= max_pi:
                count += 1
    
    return count

"""Sums over contiguous spans of a sequence."""


def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: P[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # Then sum(values[i:j]) = P[j] - P[i]
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for k in range(n):
        P[k + 1] = P[k] + values[k]
    
    # Count pairs (i, j) with i < j such that lo <= P[j] - P[i] <= hi
    # This is equivalent to: P[j] - hi <= P[i] <= P[j] - lo
    # Use Fenwick tree with coordinate compression for O(n log n)
    
    # Collect all values that need to be ranked:
    # - All prefix sums P[i]
    # - All query boundaries P[j] - hi and P[j] - lo
    all_vals = set(P)
    for pj in P:
        all_vals.add(pj - hi)
        all_vals.add(pj - lo)
    
    sorted_vals = sorted(all_vals)
    val_to_rank = {v: r + 1 for r, v in enumerate(sorted_vals)}  # 1-indexed for BIT
    m = len(sorted_vals)
    
    # Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree)
    bit = [0] * (m + 1)
    
    def bit_update(idx, delta):
        while idx <= m:
            bit[idx] += delta
            idx += idx & (-idx)
    
    def bit_query(idx):
        s = 0
        while idx > 0:
            s += bit[idx]
            idx -= idx & (-idx)
        return s
    
    def count_in_range(lo_val, hi_val):
        # Count values in [lo_val, hi_val]
        if lo_val > hi_val:
            return 0
        # Find ranks for lo_val and hi_val
        lo_rank = val_to_rank.get(lo_val, 0)
        hi_rank = val_to_rank.get(hi_val, 0)
        if lo_rank == 0 or hi_rank == 0 or lo_rank > hi_rank:
            return 0
        return bit_query(hi_rank) - bit_query(lo_rank - 1)
    
    count = 0
    # Add P[0] first (representing starting point i=0)
    bit_update(val_to_rank[P[0]], 1)
    
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        pj = P[j]
        min_pi = pj - hi
        max_pi = pj - lo
        
        # Count how many previous P[i] are in [min_pi, max_pi]
        count += count_in_range(min_pi, max_pi)
        
        # Add P[j] to the BIT for future queries
        bit_update(val_to_rank[pj], 1)
    
    return count

"""Sums over contiguous spans of a sequence."""


def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: P[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # Then sum(values[i:j]) = P[j] - P[i]
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for k in range(n):
        P[k + 1] = P[k] + values[k]
    
    # Count pairs (i, j) with i < j such that lo <= P[j] - P[i] <= hi
    # This is equivalent to: P[j] - hi <= P[i] <= P[j] - lo
    # Use Fenwick tree with coordinate compression for O(n log n)
    
    # Collect all values that need to be ranked:
    # - All prefix sums P[i]
    # - All query boundaries P[j] - hi and P[j] - lo
    all_vals = set(P)
    for pj in P:
        all_vals.add(pj - hi)
        all_vals.add(pj - lo)
    
    sorted_vals = sorted(all_vals)
    val_to_rank = {v: r + 1 for r, v in enumerate(sorted_vals)}  # 1-indexed for BIT
    m = len(sorted_vals)
    
    # Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree)
    bit = [0] * (m + 1)
    
    def bit_update(idx, delta):
        while idx <= m:
            bit[idx] += delta
            idx += idx & (-idx)
    
    def bit_query(idx):
        s = 0
        while idx > 0:
            s += bit[idx]
            idx -= idx & (-idx)
        return s
    
    def count_in_range(lo_val, hi_val):
        # Count values in [lo_val, hi_val]
        if lo_val > hi_val:
            return 0
        # Find ranks for lo_val and hi_val
        lo_rank = val_to_rank.get(lo_val, 0)
        hi_rank = val_to_rank.get(hi_val, 0)
        if lo_rank == 0 or hi_rank == 0 or lo_rank > hi_rank:
            return 0
        return bit_query(hi_rank) - bit_query(lo_rank - 1)
    
    count = 0
    # Add P[0] first (representing starting point i=0)
    bit_update(val_to_rank[P[0]], 1)
    
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        pj = P[j]
        min_pi = pj - hi
        max_pi = pj - lo
        
        # Count how many previous P[i] are in [min_pi, max_pi]
        count += count_in_range(min_pi, max_pi)
        
        # Add P[j] to the BIT for future queries
        bit_update(val_to_rank[pj], 1)
    
    return count

# span-sums

Small helpers for sums over contiguous spans of a sequence.

## `count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi)`

Returns the number of spans `values[i:j]` (`0 <= i < j <= len(values)`, i.e. non-empty runs of consecutive items)
whose sum `s` satisfies `lo <= s <= hi`. Spans at different positions count separately even if their contents are
equal.

- `values` is a list of ints (negative, zero or positive); `lo` and `hi` are ints. Both bounds are inclusive.
- An empty `values` returns `0`.
- `lo > hi` returns `0` (no sum can qualify).
- `values` is not modified.

```python
>>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)   # [1], [1, -2, 3], [-2, 3], [-2, 3, 1], [1]
5
```

`bench/inputs.json`, checks each result against `bench/expected.json`, and compares the time with the original
implementation kept in `bench/baseline.py`.

"""Run the unit tests in tests/, then the benchmark in bench.py."""
import importlib.util
import pathlib
import sys
import traceback

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))


def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run_unit_tests():
    passed = failed = 0
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "tests").glob("test_*.py")):
        try:
            module = load(path, path.stem)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"tests/{path.name} ERROR ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            continue
        for name, fn in list(vars(module).items()):
            if not (name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn)):
                continue
            try:
                fn()
            except Exception as exc:
                failed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} FAILED ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            else:
                passed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} PASSED")
    return passed, failed


def main():
    passed, failed = run_unit_tests()
    print()
    bench = load(ROOT / "bench.py", "bench")
    result = bench.main()
    print()
    print(f"{passed} passed, {failed} failed | benchmark: {result['ok']}/{result['total']} outputs match, "
          f"{result['current_ms']:.1f} ms vs baseline {result['baseline_ms']:.1f} ms, "
          f"speedup {result['speedup']:.1f}x (target {bench.TARGET_SPEEDUP:g}x)")
    return 0 if failed == 0 and result["ok"] == result["total"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Benchmark count_spans_with_sum_between on bench/inputs.json against the original implementation (bench/baseline.py)."""
import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(main())

# invoicing

Small helpers for building and printing customer invoices. Standard library only.

## Modules

- `invoicing.money`: `Decimal` money helpers. Amounts are rounded to whole cents with halves rounded
  **up, away from zero** (`0.125 -> 0.13`, `-0.125 -> -0.13`), matching the printed invoices. Floats are
  rejected; pass strings, ints or `Decimal`s.
- `invoicing.pricing`: line pricing. Lines of **10 or more units** get a 5% bulk discount; the discounted
  line amount is rounded to the cent.
- `invoicing.currency`: exchange rates (`RATES`, in units of the currency per 1 EUR). `to_eur(amount, currency)`
  gives the EUR value rounded to the cent (used for EUR reporting). `convert(amount, src, dst)` converts at full
  precision through EUR (`amount / RATES[src] * RATES[dst]`) and rounds to the cent **once, at the end**.
- `invoicing.invoice`: `Invoice` (subtotal, VAT at 20% by default, total, `total_eur()` for reporting) and
  `paginate(lines, per_page)`, which splits invoice lines into printed pages of at most `per_page` lines, in
  order. Every line appears on exactly one page; an invoice with no lines has no pages. An invoice has a
  currency (EUR by default); a line can be priced in another currency, in which case its line amount (priced as
  above, in the price currency) is converted to the invoice currency with `convert`.

## Example

```python
from invoicing.invoice import Invoice

inv = Invoice("INV-0042")
inv.add("Widget", 12, "2.50")
inv.add("Shipping", 1, "4.99")
inv.add("Adapter", 2, "7.35", price_currency="GBP")
print(inv.subtotal(), inv.tax(), inv.total())
```

## Running the tests

    python -B run_tests.py

    return start_dir, pattern


def main():

    return 0 if result.wasSuccessful() else 1

import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)

class FenwickTree:
    """Binary Indexed Tree for efficient prefix sum queries and updates."""
    
    def __init__(self, size):
        self.size = size
        self.tree = [0] * (size + 1)
    
    def update(self, index, delta=1):
        """Add delta to element at index (1-indexed)."""
        while index <= self.size:
            self.tree[index] += delta
            index += index & (-index)
    
    def query(self, index):
        """Return sum of elements from 1 to index (inclusive, 1-indexed)."""
        result = 0
        while index > 0:
            result += self.tree[index]
            index -= index & (-index)
        return result
    
    def query_range(self, left, right):
        """Return sum of elements from left to right (inclusive, 1-indexed)."""
        if left > right:
            return 0
        return self.query(right) - self.query(left - 1)


def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5

    # Handle edge cases
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: prefix[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # Sum of values[i:j] = prefix[j] - prefix[i]
    # We need: lo <= prefix[j] - prefix[i] <= hi
    # Which means: prefix[j] - hi <= prefix[i] <= prefix[j] - lo
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for k in range(n):
        prefix[k + 1] = prefix[k] + values[k]
    
    # Coordinate compression for Fenwick tree
    # We need to track all possible values of prefix[i] and also prefix[j] - lo, prefix[j] - hi
    sorted_unique = sorted(set(prefix))
    rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted_unique)}  # 1-indexed ranks
    m = len(sorted_unique)
    
    def get_rank_lowest_at_least(val):
        """Get the rank of the smallest value >= val, or m+1 if none exists."""
        import bisect
        idx = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_unique, val)
        if idx < m:
            return rank[sorted_unique[idx]]
        return m + 1
    
    def get_rank_highest_at_most(val):
        """Get the rank of the largest value <= val, or 0 if none exists."""
        import bisect
        idx = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_unique, val) - 1
        if idx >= 0:
            return rank[sorted_unique[idx]]
        return 0
    
    ft = FenwickTree(m)
    count = 0
    
    # Process each position j from 1 to n
    # At step j, we've added prefix[0..j-1] to the Fenwick tree
    # We query for prefix[i] in [prefix[j] - hi, prefix[j] - lo]
    
    # Add prefix[0] = 0 first
    ft.update(rank[prefix[0]])
    
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        pj = prefix[j]
        # We need prefix[i] in range [pj - hi, pj - lo]
        min_val = pj - hi
        max_val = pj - lo
        
        left_rank = get_rank_lowest_at_least(min_val)
        right_rank = get_rank_highest_at_most(max_val)
        
        if left_rank <= right_rank:
            count += ft.query_range(left_rank, right_rank)
        
        # Add current prefix to Fenwick tree for future queries
        ft.update(rank[pj])
    
    return count

# span-sums

Small helpers for sums over contiguous spans of a sequence.

## `count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi)`

Returns the number of spans `values[i:j]` (`0 <= i < j <= len(values)`, i.e. non-empty runs of consecutive items)
whose sum `s` satisfies `lo <= s <= hi`. Spans at different positions count separately even if their contents are
equal.

- `values` is a list of ints (negative, zero or positive); `lo` and `hi` are ints. Both bounds are inclusive.
- An empty `values` returns `0`.
- `lo > hi` returns `0` (no sum can qualify).
- `values` is not modified.

"""Run the unit tests in tests/, then the benchmark in bench.py."""
import importlib.util
import pathlib
import sys
import traceback

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))


def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run_unit_tests():
    passed = failed = 0
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "tests").glob("test_*.py")):
        try:
            module = load(path, path.stem)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"tests/{path.name} ERROR ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            continue
        for name, fn in list(vars(module).items()):
            if not (name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn)):
                continue
            try:
                fn()
            except Exception as exc:
                failed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} FAILED ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            else:
                passed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} PASSED")
    return passed, failed


def main():
    passed, failed = run_unit_tests()
    print()
    bench = load(ROOT / "bench.py", "bench")
    result = bench.main()
    print()
    print(f"{passed} passed, {failed} failed | benchmark: {result['ok']}/{result['total']} outputs match, "
          f"{result['current_ms']:.1f} ms vs baseline {result['baseline_ms']:.1f} ms, "
          f"speedup {result['speedup']:.1f}x (target {bench.TARGET_SPEEDUP:g}x)")
    return 0 if failed == 0 and result["ok"] == result["total"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Benchmark count_spans_with_sum_between on bench/inputs.json against the original implementation (bench/baseline.py)."""
import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(main())

    return time.perf_counter() - start, out

- which means prefix_sum[j] - hi <= prefix_sum[i] <= prefix_sum[j] - lo

2. For each j from 1 to n:

def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: P[0] = 0, P[k] = sum(values[:k])
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + values[i]
    
    # Coordinate compression for all relevant prefix sum values
    # We need to query ranges [P[j] - hi, P[j] - lo] for each j
    # So we need all P values and all P[j] - hi, P[j] - lo values
    
    all_values = set(P)
    for p in P:
        all_values.add(p - hi)
        all_values.add(p - lo)
    
    sorted_vals = sorted(all_values)
    rank = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(sorted_vals)}
    
    # Fenwick tree to count occurrences
    fenwick = [0] * (len(sorted_vals) + 1)
    
    def update(idx, delta):
        idx += 1
        while idx < len(fenwick):
            fenwick[idx] += delta
            idx += idx & (-idx)
    
    def query(idx):
        idx += 1
        s = 0
        while idx > 0:
            s += fenwick[idx]
            idx -= idx & (-idx)
        return s

    for j in range(1, n + 1):

        low_bound = P[j] - hi
        high_bound = P[j] - lo

        count += query(rank[high_bound]) - query(rank[low_bound] - 1)
        
        # Add current prefix sum to Fenwick tree
        update(rank[P[j]], 1)

# span-sums

Small helpers for sums over contiguous spans of a sequence.

## `count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi)`

Returns the number of spans `values[i:j]` (`0 <= i < j <= len(values)`, i.e. non-empty runs of consecutive items)
whose sum `s` satisfies `lo <= s <= hi`. Spans at different positions count separately even if their contents are
equal.

- `values` is a list of ints (negative, zero or positive); `lo` and `hi` are ints. Both bounds are inclusive.
- An empty `values` returns `0`.
- `lo > hi` returns `0` (no sum can qualify).
- `values` is not modified.

```python
>>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)   # [1], [1, -2, 3], [-2, 3], [-2, 3, 1], [1]
5
```

"""Run the unit tests in tests/, then the benchmark in bench.py."""
import importlib.util
import pathlib
import sys
import traceback

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))


def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run_unit_tests():
    passed = failed = 0
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "tests").glob("test_*.py")):
        try:
            module = load(path, path.stem)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"tests/{path.name} ERROR ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            continue
        for name, fn in list(vars(module).items()):
            if not (name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn)):
                continue
            try:
                fn()
            except Exception as exc:
                failed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} FAILED ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            else:
                passed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} PASSED")
    return passed, failed


def main():
    passed, failed = run_unit_tests()
    print()
    bench = load(ROOT / "bench.py", "bench")
    result = bench.main()
    print()
    print(f"{passed} passed, {failed} failed | benchmark: {result['ok']}/{result['total']} outputs match, "
          f"{result['current_ms']:.1f} ms vs baseline {result['baseline_ms']:.1f} ms, "
          f"speedup {result['speedup']:.1f}x (target {bench.TARGET_SPEEDUP:g}x)")
    return 0 if failed == 0 and result["ok"] == result["total"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Benchmark count_spans_with_sum_between on bench/inputs.json against the original implementation (bench/baseline.py)."""
import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(main())

# invoicing

Small helpers for building and printing customer invoices. Standard library only.

## Modules

- `invoicing.money`: `Decimal` money helpers. Amounts are rounded to whole cents with halves rounded
  **up, away from zero** (`0.125 -> 0.13`, `-0.125 -> -0.13`), matching the printed invoices. Floats are
  rejected; pass strings, ints or `Decimal`s.
- `invoicing.pricing`: line pricing. Lines of **10 or more units** get a 5% bulk discount; the discounted
  line amount is rounded to the cent.
- `invoicing.currency`: exchange rates (`RATES`, in units of the currency per 1 EUR). `to_eur(amount, currency)`
  gives the EUR value rounded to the cent (used for EUR reporting). `convert(amount, src, dst)` converts at full
  precision through EUR (`amount / RATES[src] * RATES[dst]`) and rounds to the cent **once, at the end**.
- `invoicing.invoice`: `Invoice` (subtotal, VAT at 20% by default, total, `total_eur()` for reporting) and
  `paginate(lines, per_page)`, which splits invoice lines into printed pages of at most `per_page` lines, in
  order. Every line appears on exactly one page; an invoice with no lines has no pages. An invoice has a
  currency (EUR by default); a line can be priced in another currency, in which case its line amount (priced as
  above, in the price currency) is converted to the invoice currency with `convert`.

## Example

```python
from invoicing.invoice import Invoice

inv = Invoice("INV-0042")
inv.add("Widget", 12, "2.50")
inv.add("Shipping", 1, "4.99")
inv.add("Adapter", 2, "7.35", price_currency="GBP")
print(inv.subtotal(), inv.tax(), inv.total())
```

## Running the tests

    python -B run_tests.py

"""Run the invoicing test suite: python -B run_tests.py"""
import configparser
import sys
import unittest

CONFIG = "setup.cfg"


def discovery_settings(path=CONFIG):
    cfg = configparser.ConfigParser()
    cfg.read(path)
    start_dir = cfg.get("tool:unittest", "start_dir", fallback="tests")
    pattern = cfg.get("tool:unittest", "pattern", fallback="test_*.py")
    return start_dir, pattern


def main():
    start_dir, pattern = discovery_settings()
    suite = unittest.TestLoader().discover(start_dir, pattern=pattern, top_level_dir=".")
    result = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2).run(suite)
    return 0 if result.wasSuccessful() else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

import unittest
from decimal import Decimal

from invoicing.invoice import Invoice, paginate


class InvoiceTotalsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_subtotal_tax_total(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-1")
        inv.add("Widget", 2, "10.00")
        inv.add("Shipping", 1, "5.25")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("25.25"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.tax(), Decimal("5.05"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("30.30"))

    def test_empty_invoice(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-2")
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("0.00"))


class ForeignCurrencyTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_lines_priced_in_another_currency(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-3", currency="USD")
        inv.add("Adapter", 3, "4.99", price_currency="GBP")
        inv.add("Cable", 12, "12.50", price_currency="GBP")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("199.83"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.tax(), Decimal("39.97"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("239.80"))

    def test_mixed_currency_invoice(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-4", currency="GBP")
        inv.add("Licence", 1, "8.75", price_currency="USD")
        inv.add("Support", 1, "4.99", price_currency="CHF")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("11.43"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.total(), Decimal("13.72"))

    def test_chf_invoice(self):
        inv = Invoice("INV-5", currency="CHF")
        inv.add("Licence", 1, "4.99", price_currency="USD")
        inv.add("Adapter", 1, "3.20", price_currency="GBP")
        self.assertEqual(inv.subtotal(), Decimal("7.86"))
        self.assertEqual(inv.tax(), Decimal("1.57"))


class PaginateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_exact_multiple(self):
        self.assertEqual(paginate(["a", "b", "c", "d"], 2), [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"]])

    def test_keeps_last_partial_page(self):
        self.assertEqual(paginate(["a", "b", "c", "d", "e"], 2), [["a", "b"], ["c", "d"], ["e"]])

    def test_single_line(self):
        self.assertEqual(paginate(["a"], 3), [["a"]])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

def parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into a list of records, each a list of field strings."""

        rows.append(line.split(","))
    return rows

"""Small CSV parsing helper used by the reporting scripts."""


def parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]:
    """Parse CSV text into a list of records, each a list of field strings."""
    rows = []
    i = 0
    n = len(text)
    
    while i < n:
        # Skip any leading whitespace/newlines between rows
        if text[i] == '\r':
            i += 1
            if i < n and text[i] == '\n':
                i += 1
            continue
        elif text[i] == '\n':
            i += 1
            continue
        
        # Start a new row
        row = []
        
        while True:
            # Check for end of row (newline)
            if i >= n:
                break
            if text[i] == '\r':
                i += 1
                if i < n and text[i] == '\n':
                    i += 1
                break
            elif text[i] == '\n':
                i += 1
                break
            
            # Parse a field
            if text[i] == '"':
                # Quoted field
                i += 1  # Skip opening quote
                field = ""
                while i < n:
                    if text[i] == '"':
                        if i + 1 < n and text[i + 1] == '"':
                            # Escaped quote
                            field += '"'
                            i += 2
                        else:
                            # End of quoted field
                            i += 1
                            # Skip to comma or end of row
                            while i < n and text[i] not in ',\r\n':
                                i += 1
                            break
                    else:
                        field += text[i]
                        i += 1
                row.append(field)
            else:
                # Unquoted field - read until comma or newline
                field = ""
                while i < n and text[i] not in ',\r\n':
                    field += text[i]
                    i += 1
                row.append(field)
            
            # After field, check what comes next
            if i >= n:
                break
            if text[i] == ',':
                i += 1  # Skip comma
                # Continue to next field
            else:
                # Hit newline - already handled above
                break
        
        # If we broke out because of newline after a comma, we need to check
        # Actually, let's re-check: if the last character before newline was a comma
        # We need to look back at what happened
        
        # Add the row
        rows.append(row)
    
    return rows

# csvparse

`csvparse.parse(text: str) -> list[list[str]]` turns CSV text into a list of records, where each record is a
list of field strings.

## Supported format

- The delimiter is always a comma (`,`).

import json
import sys
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
FIXTURES = ROOT / "tests" / "fixtures"


def short(value, limit=160):
    text = json.dumps(value, default=repr)
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit] + "..."


def main():
    sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))
    try:
        from csvparse import parse
    except Exception:
        print("ERROR importing csvparse.py")
        for line in traceback.format_exc().strip().splitlines()[-4:]:
            print("    " + line)
        print("========== 1 error ==========")
        return 1
    passed = failed = 0
    for csv_path in sorted(FIXTURES.glob("*.csv")):
        name = "tests/fixtures/" + csv_path.name
        with open(csv_path, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            text = fh.read()
        expected = json.loads(csv_path.with_suffix(".json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        try:
            got = parse(text)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(name + " FAILED")
            print("    " + type(exc).__name__ + ": " + str(exc)[:200])
            continue
        if got == expected:
            passed += 1
            print(name + " PASSED")
        else:
            failed += 1
            print(name + " FAILED")
            print("    input:    " + short(text))
            print("    expected: " + short(expected))
            print("    got:      " + short(got))
    if failed:
        print("========== %d failed, %d passed ==========" % (failed, passed))
    else:
        print("========== %d passed ==========" % passed)
    return 1 if failed else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Sums over contiguous spans of a sequence."""

import bisect


def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    # Handle edge cases
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: prefix[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # Then sum(values[i:j]) = prefix[j] - prefix[i]
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + values[i]
    
    # For each j from 1 to n, we need to count i from 0 to j-1 such that:
    # lo <= prefix[j] - prefix[i] <= hi
    # which means: prefix[j] - hi <= prefix[i] <= prefix[j] - lo
    
    # Coordinate compression for Fenwick tree
    sorted_unique = sorted(set(prefix))
    rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted_unique)}  # 1-indexed
    m = len(sorted_unique)
    
    # Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree), 1-indexed
    bit = [0] * (m + 1)
    
    def update(i, delta=1):
        """Add delta to position i."""
        while i <= m:
            bit[i] += delta
            i += i & (-i)
    
    def query(i):
        """Return sum from position 1 to i."""
        s = 0
        while i > 0:
            s += bit[i]
            i -= i & (-i)
        return s
    
    def query_range(l, r):
        """Return sum from position l to r (inclusive)."""
        if l > r:
            return 0
        return query(r) - query(l - 1)
    
    count = 0
    
    # Insert prefix[0] into the Fenwick tree (represents empty prefix before first element)
    update(rank[prefix[0]])
    
    # Process each position j from 1 to n
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        pj = prefix[j]
        
        # We need prefix[i] in range [pj - hi, pj - lo] for i < j
        target_lo = pj - hi
        target_hi = pj - lo
        
        # Find indices in sorted_unique for binary search
        idx_lo = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_unique, target_lo)
        idx_hi = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_unique, target_hi) - 1
        
        # Convert to 1-indexed ranks for Fenwick tree
        rank_lo = idx_lo + 1
        rank_hi = idx_hi + 1
        
        # Count how many previous prefix values fall in the valid range
        if rank_lo <= rank_hi:
            count += query_range(rank_lo, rank_hi)
        
        # Add current prefix value to the Fenwick tree
        update(rank[pj])
    
    return count

"""Sums over contiguous spans of a sequence."""

import bisect


def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    # Handle edge cases
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    n = len(values)
    
    # Compute prefix sums: prefix[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    # Then sum(values[i:j]) = prefix[j] - prefix[i]
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + values[i]
    
    # For each j from 1 to n, we need to count i from 0 to j-1 such that:
    # lo <= prefix[j] - prefix[i] <= hi
    # which means: prefix[j] - hi <= prefix[i] <= prefix[j] - lo
    
    # Coordinate compression for Fenwick tree
    sorted_unique = sorted(set(prefix))
    rank = {v: i + 1 for i, v in enumerate(sorted_unique)}  # 1-indexed
    m = len(sorted_unique)
    
    # Fenwick tree (Binary Indexed Tree), 1-indexed
    bit = [0] * (m + 1)
    
    def update(i, delta=1):
        """Add delta to position i."""
        while i <= m:
            bit[i] += delta
            i += i & (-i)
    
    def query(i):
        """Return sum from position 1 to i."""
        s = 0
        while i > 0:
            s += bit[i]
            i -= i & (-i)
        return s
    
    def query_range(l, r):
        """Return sum from position l to r (inclusive)."""
        if l > r:
            return 0
        return query(r) - query(l - 1)
    
    count = 0
    
    # Insert prefix[0] into the Fenwick tree (represents empty prefix before first element)
    update(rank[prefix[0]])
    
    # Process each position j from 1 to n
    for j in range(1, n + 1):
        pj = prefix[j]
        
        # We need prefix[i] in range [pj - hi, pj - lo] for i < j
        target_lo = pj - hi
        target_hi = pj - lo
        
        # Find indices in sorted_unique for binary search
        idx_lo = bisect.bisect_left(sorted_unique, target_lo)
        idx_hi = bisect.bisect_right(sorted_unique, target_hi) - 1
        
        # Convert to 1-indexed ranks for Fenwick tree
        rank_lo = idx_lo + 1
        rank_hi = idx_hi + 1
        
        # Count how many previous prefix values fall in the valid range
        if rank_lo <= rank_hi:
            count += query_range(rank_lo, rank_hi)
        
        # Add current prefix value to the Fenwick tree
        update(rank[pj])
    
    return count

# span-sums

Small helpers for sums over contiguous spans of a sequence.

## `count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi)`

Returns the number of spans `values[i:j]` (`0 <= i < j <= len(values)`, i.e. non-empty runs of consecutive items)
whose sum `s` satisfies `lo <= s <= hi`. Spans at different positions count separately even if their contents are
equal.

- `values` is a list of ints (negative, zero or positive); `lo` and `hi` are ints. Both bounds are inclusive.
- An empty `values` returns `0`.
- `lo > hi` returns `0` (no sum can qualify).
- `values` is not modified.

```python
>>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)   # [1], [1, -2, 3], [-2, 3], [-2, 3, 1], [1]
5
```

## Tests and benchmark

    python -B run_tests.py

runs the unit tests in `tests/`, then `bench.py`, which times `count_spans_with_sum_between` on the benchmark inputs in
`bench/inputs.json`, checks each result against `bench/expected.json`, and compares the time with the original
implementation kept in `bench/baseline.py`.

"""Run the unit tests in tests/, then the benchmark in bench.py."""
import importlib.util
import pathlib
import sys
import traceback

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))


def load(path, name):
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module


def run_unit_tests():
    passed = failed = 0
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "tests").glob("test_*.py")):
        try:
            module = load(path, path.stem)
        except Exception as exc:
            failed += 1
            print(f"tests/{path.name} ERROR ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            continue
        for name, fn in list(vars(module).items()):
            if not (name.startswith("test_") and callable(fn)):
                continue
            try:
                fn()
            except Exception as exc:
                failed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} FAILED ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
            else:
                passed += 1
                print(f"tests/{path.name}::{name} PASSED")
    return passed, failed


def main():
    passed, failed = run_unit_tests()
    print()
    bench = load(ROOT / "bench.py", "bench")
    result = bench.main()
    print()
    print(f"{passed} passed, {failed} failed | benchmark: {result['ok']}/{result['total']} outputs match, "
          f"{result['current_ms']:.1f} ms vs baseline {result['baseline_ms']:.1f} ms, "
          f"speedup {result['speedup']:.1f}x (target {bench.TARGET_SPEEDUP:g}x)")
    return 0 if failed == 0 and result["ok"] == result["total"] else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

"""Benchmark count_spans_with_sum_between on bench/inputs.json against the original implementation (bench/baseline.py)."""
import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print(main())

"""Money helpers. All amounts are Decimals rounded to whole cents."""
from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def to_decimal(value):
    """Convert an int, str or Decimal to Decimal. Floats are rejected to avoid binary rounding surprises."""
    if isinstance(value, float):
        raise TypeError("use str or Decimal for money amounts, not float")
    return Decimal(value)


def round_money(value):
    """Round an amount to whole cents (half away from zero)."""
    d = to_decimal(value)
    # Scale to cents
    scaled = d * 100
    # Use ROUND_DOWN to truncate toward zero
    truncated = scaled.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_DOWN)
    remainder = abs(scaled - truncated)
    
    # Round half away from zero
    if remainder >= Decimal("0.5"):
        # Half or more - round away from zero
        if scaled > 0:
            truncated += 1
        else:
            truncated -= 1
    
    return truncated / 100


def format_money(value, currency="EUR"):
    """Format an amount for printing, e.g. '1,234.50 EUR'."""
    return f"{round_money(value):,.2f} {currency}"

# invoicing

Small helpers for building and printing customer invoices. Standard library only.

## Modules

- `invoicing.money`: `Decimal` money helpers. Amounts are rounded to whole cents with halves rounded
  **up, away from zero** (`0.125 -> 0.13`, `-0.125 -> -0.13`), matching the printed invoices. Floats are
  rejected; pass strings, ints or `Decimal`s.
- `invoicing.pricing`: line pricing. Lines of **10 or more units** get a 5% bulk discount; the discounted
  line amount is rounded to the cent.
- `invoicing.currency`: exchange rates (`RATES`, in units of the currency per 1 EUR). `to_eur(amount, currency)`
  gives the EUR value rounded to the cent (used for EUR reporting). `convert(amount, src, dst)` converts at full
  precision through EUR (`amount / RATES[src] * RATES[dst]`) and rounds to the cent **once, at the end**.
- `invoicing.invoice`: `Invoice` (subtotal, VAT at 20% by default, total, `total_eur()` for reporting) and

"""Money helpers. All amounts are Decimals rounded to whole cents."""
from decimal import ROUND_DOWN, Decimal

CENT = Decimal("0.01")


def to_decimal(value):
    """Convert an int, str or Decimal to Decimal. Floats are rejected to avoid binary rounding surprises."""
    if isinstance(value, float):
        raise TypeError("use str or Decimal for money amounts, not float")
    return Decimal(value)


def round_money(value):
    """Round an amount to whole cents (half away from zero)."""
    d = to_decimal(value)
    # Scale to cents
    scaled = d * 100
    # Use ROUND_DOWN to truncate toward zero
    truncated = scaled.to_integral_value(rounding=ROUND_DOWN)
    remainder = abs(scaled - truncated)
    
    # Round half away from zero
    if remainder >= Decimal("0.5"):
        # Half or more - round away from zero
        if scaled > 0:
            truncated += 1
        else:
            truncated -= 1
    
    return truncated / 100


def format_money(value, currency="EUR"):
    """Format an amount for printing, e.g. '1,234.50 EUR'."""
    return f"{round_money(value):,.2f} {currency}"

def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    count = 0
    n = len(values)
    for i in range(n):
        for j in range(i + 1, n + 1):
            if lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi:
                count += 1
    return count

"""Benchmark count_spans_with_sum_between on bench/inputs.json against the original implementation (bench/baseline.py)."""
import importlib.util
import json
import pathlib
import statistics
import time

ROOT = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
REPEATS = 5            # timed calls per case for the current implementation (median is reported)
BASELINE_REPEATS = 3   # timed calls per case for the baseline
TARGET_SPEEDUP = 60


def load_baseline():
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("baseline", ROOT / "bench" / "baseline.py")
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    return module.count_spans_with_sum_between


def timed(fn, values, lo, hi):
    values = list(values)
    start = time.perf_counter()
    try:
        out = fn(values, lo, hi)
    except Exception as exc:
        out = exc
    return time.perf_counter() - start, out


def main():
    cases = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "inputs.json").read_text())["cases"]
    expected = json.loads((ROOT / "bench" / "expected.json").read_text())
    baseline = load_baseline()
    try:
        from span_sums import count_spans_with_sum_between as current
    except Exception as exc:
        print(f"bench: could not import span_sums ({type(exc).__name__}: {exc})")
        current = None
    ok = 0
    base_total = cur_total = 0.0
    for case in cases:
        name, lo, hi, values = case["name"], case["lo"], case["hi"], case["values"]
        base = statistics.median(timed(baseline, values, lo, hi)[0] for _ in range(BASELINE_REPEATS))
        if current is None:
            cur, good = base, False
        else:
            runs = [timed(current, values, lo, hi) for _ in range(REPEATS)]
            cur = statistics.median(t for t, _ in runs)
            good = all(out == expected[name] for _, out in runs)
        ok += good
        base_total += base
        cur_total += cur
        print(f"bench {name} (n={len(values)}, lo={lo}, hi={hi}): baseline {base * 1000:.2f} ms, "
              f"current {cur * 1000:.2f} ms, {base / max(cur, 1e-9):.1f}x, output {'OK' if good else 'MISMATCH'}")
    speedup = base_total / max(cur_total, 1e-9)
    return dict(ok=ok, total=len(cases), baseline_ms=base_total * 1000, current_ms=cur_total * 1000, speedup=speedup)


if __name__ == "__main__":

def count_spans_with_sum_between(values, lo, hi):
    """Return how many spans of ``values`` have a sum between ``lo`` and ``hi``, inclusive.

    A span is a non-empty run of consecutive items ``values[i:j]`` with ``0 <= i < j <= len(values)``. Spans
    at different positions are counted separately, even if their contents are equal. ``values`` is a list of
    ints (negative, zero or positive) and ``lo`` and ``hi`` are ints; a span counts when
    ``lo <= sum(values[i:j]) <= hi``.

    Edge cases:
      - an empty ``values`` returns ``0``.
      - ``lo > hi`` returns ``0`` (no sum can qualify).
    ``values`` is not modified.

    >>> count_spans_with_sum_between([1, -2, 3, 1], 1, 2)
    5
    """
    if not values or lo > hi:
        return 0
    
    # Build prefix sums: P[0] = 0, P[k] = sum(values[0:k])
    n = len(values)
    P = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i in range(n):
        P[i + 1] = P[i] + values[i]
    
    # Count pairs (i, j) with i < j and lo <= P[j] - P[i] <= hi
    # This is equivalent to: P[j] - hi <= P[i] <= P[j] - lo
    return _count_in_range(P, lo, hi)


def _count_in_range(P, lo, hi):
    """Count pairs (i,j) with i<j and lo <= P[j]-P[i] <= hi using merge sort."""
    n = len(P)
    indices = list(range(n))
    temp = [0] * n
    count = 0
    
    def merge_sort(left, right):
        nonlocal count
        if right - left <= 1:
            return
        
        mid = (left + right) // 2
        merge_sort(left, mid)
        merge_sort(mid, right)
        
        # Count valid pairs where i in [left, mid) and j in [mid, right)
        # For each j in [mid, right), count i in [left, mid) where P[j]-hi <= P[i] <= P[j]-lo
        j = mid
        l_bound = left
        r_bound = left
        
        while j < right:
            pj_hi = P[indices[j]] - hi
            pj_lo = P[indices[j]] - lo
            
            # Move l_bound to first element >= pj_hi
            while l_bound < mid and P[indices[l_bound]] < pj_hi:
                l_bound += 1
            
            # Move r_bound to first element > pj_lo
            while r_bound < mid and P[indices[r_bound]] <= pj_lo:
                r_bound += 1
            
            count += (r_bound - l_bound)
            j += 1
        
        # Merge step
        i, j = left, mid
        idx = left
        while i < mid and j < right:
            if P[indices[i]] <= P[indices[j]]:
                temp[idx] = indices[i]
                i += 1
            else:
                temp[idx] = indices[j]
                j += 1
            idx += 1
        while i < mid:
            temp[idx] = indices[i]
            i += 1
            idx += 1
        while j < right:
            temp[idx] = indices[j]
            j += 1
            idx += 1
        
        for k in range(left, right):
            indices[k] = temp[k]
    
    merge_sort(0, n)
    return count
